_why: THE VANILLA BASELINE ON THE ELEVEN-TAG LIST (open item 3). The register's PI and PP are read on the INTERSECTION of an arm's markets and vanilla's, and the pinned n=16 baseline `20260821_131149` carries only the SEVEN tags — so the German and Belgian markets a modern arm now instruments are excluded from the price indices, and criteria.mjs prints that it dropped them. This supplies the missing side of the ratio.
_arm: {kind: control} — VANILLA + telemetry and nothing else. An engine/reference question belongs on the vanilla arm (CLAUDE.md's arm discipline), and this IS the reference.
_what_it_also_buys: SAVE-SUMMARY v9. These runs are the first vanilla ones harvested since the schema gained `goods_sales`, `goods_cost`, `salary_w` and `taxes` per building type (FINDINGS F152 §10), so they are the first vanilla reference on which a wages-inclusive profit% is EXACT rather than repaired through a price multiplier. Past sessions cannot be back-filled — the harvester reaps the .v3.
_n: THREE, not sixteen. The pinned n=16 baseline stays the reference for everything it already answers (GDP, W, U*, H, the 1836 anchor CI, the σ constants); this batch exists to add TWO markets to the price basis and to carry v9. Three seeds give a usable median for a price index without spending forty hours. ⚠ It does NOT replace the n=16 baseline and must never be quoted as the vanilla reference for the register's other lines — its own seed spread is far too small for that.
_reading_it: After it lands, `criteria.mjs --van <this session>` prints a price basis of six markets instead of four. ⚠ Compare a book against ONE vanilla reference at a time and say which; a loss computed against this baseline is NOT comparable to one computed against the n=16 one, because the price basis differs.
_cost: 3 runs x 1836->1936. Vanilla runs at roughly 2h20 each, so about 7 hours.
